fixes.explanation: Treasures is a shiny guess, and I'm a cookie stamper, so I respect shiny. But verse 7 says, “She defiled herself with all the idols of those for whom she lusted.” The word is idols, and no gold gets counted anywhere in that verse. I think it's a hard thing to read, and it's easy to reach for something sparkly instead.

Gifts is a kind guess, friend, like showing up to a party with a plate of cookies. But nobody in verse 16 gets handed a present. It says, “At the sight of them, she lusted for them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.” She sends messengers, so the thing traveling to Chaldea is word, not a wrapped box.

Soldiers is a big, loud guess, and I almost heard the trumpets, friend. But verse 27 says, “So I will put an end to your indecency and prostitution, which began in the land of Egypt…” The thing God says He'll end is that. No soldiers get named in that verse, and no crown shows up either.

Taking over land sounds like something you'd hear in a big dispute, friend, but this verse isn't one. Verse 31 says, “Because you have followed the path of your sister, I will put her cup into your hand.” God points at the path she walked, not at any ground she grabbed. Same path, same cup.

Never hearing His word is a tempting guess, friend, like blaming a missed text on bad signal. But verse 35 says, “Because you have forgotten Me and have cast Me behind your back…” Those are God's own words, and they sound like someone who knew Him and turned away. Hearing never comes up in that verse.
